policy: Offline-first research prototype. Sentinel does not ingest NASA datasets or live NASA telemetry. It applies a NASA-published CO₂ reference to synthetic scenario readings; NASA publications provide context, not clinical validation.

steps.label: NASA reference
steps.description: NASA OCHMO-TB-004 summarizes NASA-STD-3001 Volume 2, requirement V2 6004: the habitable-volume CO₂ partial pressure is averaged over one hour and must be no greater than 3 mmHg.

steps.label: Implemented rule
steps.description: Sentinel uses 3.0 mmHg as the comparison limit and evaluates a time-weighted rolling average after a complete 60-minute sample window.

steps.label: Scenario input
steps.description: The CO₂ readings and crew measurements come from local synthetic scenario files. They are not NASA telemetry or values extracted from a NASA dataset.

steps.label: What the result means
steps.description: The alert demonstrates applying a published NASA reference to synthetic input; it is not a measurement of a real habitat or a compliance determination.

data_layers.label: NASA reference
data_layers.description: Published requirement or technical evidence from NASA; review the scope and limitations of each source.

data_layers.label: Prototype inference
data_layers.description: Project rule motivated by published evidence, but not validated as a diagnostic or predictive method.

data_layers.label: Synthetic data
data_layers.description: Simulated crew values and symptoms. They are not real astronaut telemetry or NASA study data.

scenario_data.description: Ana's profile, symptoms, local CO₂, ventilation, heart rate, and timeline are generated for this demonstration. The local fan changes only Ana's synthetic local CO₂ and airflow with an illustrative 5-minute linear ramp down to 1.8 mmHg. The separate module ventilation action uses an illustrative 10-minute linear ramp down to 2.4 mmHg. These targets and timings do not come from NASA and were not validated; module alert resolution depends on the hourly rolling average.
scenario_data.threshold_note: Illustrative project parameter, not an individual NASA threshold or clinical limit.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
sources.supports: Explains that reduced convection in microgravity can allow local CO₂ pockets near the nose and mouth. It cites a computational fluid dynamics analysis that estimated levels above 9 mmHg near the mouth and chin of a sleeping person within 10 minutes without adequate ventilation; targeted face fans are used in sleep areas.
sources.limitations: The report states that there are few real local exposure measurements and that individual susceptibility to CO₂ cannot be concluded. The source supports physical plausibility, not validation of the Sentinel inference.

sources.title: Relationship Between Carbon Dioxide Levels and Reported Congestion and Headaches on the International Space Station
sources.supports: Reports an association between ISS CO₂ levels and reports of congestion and headache. For each 1 mmHg increase, the odds of reporting congestion doubled; the summary estimates that the 7-day average should remain below 1.5 mmHg to keep congestion risk below 1%.
sources.limitations: The doubled-odds result refers to congestion, not headache. The analysis uses ambient CO₂ measurements over 24-hour and 7-day periods; it does not establish a temporal sequence between congestion and headache or validate the instantaneous local threshold used in this prototype.

sources.title: Carbon Dioxide (CO2)
sources.supports: Summarizes NASA-STD-3001 Volume 2 Rev D requirement V2 6004: average partial pressure of CO₂ in one hour in the habitable volume at or below 3 mmHg. It also discusses a 7-day average below 2.5 mmHg to keep headache risk below 1%.
sources.limitations: Sentinel computes a time-weighted 60-minute average using synthetic readings. This is not habitat measurement or compliance determination. This note does not specify the personal threshold of 2.1 mmHg.

sources.title: Earth Independent Medical Operations (EIMO)
sources.supports: Describes the need for progressively autonomous operational medical support and a clinical decision support system for contingencies in which Earth support is delayed or unavailable.
sources.limitations: This is conceptual and operational context, not a clinical guideline or validation of Sentinel algorithms.

module_co2_limit.note: The alert uses a time-weighted rolling average over 60 simulated minutes, waits for a full window, and resets coverage after a missing, negative, non-finite, malformed reading or a sampling gap larger than 1.5 simulated minutes. The readings are synthetic; this is not habitat compliance measurement.

co2_pocket_inference.classification: Physically plausible hypothesis supported by NASA source; prototype inference
co2_pocket_inference.note: The report supports local pocket plausibility. Sentinel infers risk using synthetic local CO₂, immobility, and ventilation; it does not measure or clinically validate a pocket.

co2_warning_congestion.note: The study reports an association with ISS ambient CO₂; the doubled-odds result is for congestion and uses 24-hour/7-day exposure measures, not the instantaneous local value in this scenario.

co2_warning_headache.note: CO₂ has been associated with headache reports on the ISS, but this synthetic local reading and symptom do not establish cause or diagnosis.

spo2_critical.note: The threshold is configured for this prototype and is not supported by the NASA sources listed here.

hr_critical.note: The threshold is configured for this prototype and is not supported by the NASA sources listed here.
